name: Nectarine
grown_as: A smooth-skinned peach, grown as a small tree, often fan-trained against a warm wall or kept in a pot, sometimes under glass. William grows 'Humboldt' and 'John Rivers'. Both have pink blossom; fruit colour varies a little between them.
habit: A small open deciduous tree or wall fan, 2 to 4 m. Smooth reddish-brown young shoots, red on the sunny side. Fruits on shoots that grew the year before, not on spurs.

leaf.outline: Long and narrow, lance-shaped, 8 to 15 cm long and only 2 to 4 cm wide, often folded a little along the midrib and arching downward
leaf.tip: Drawn out to a long fine point
leaf.margin: Finely and sharply toothed all round
leaf.veins: A strong pale midrib and many fine, close side veins
leaf.surface: Smooth, hairless and glossy on both sides; often puckered, thickened and red-blistered where peach leaf curl strikes in spring
leaf.stalk: Short, about 1 cm, with small glands near the blade

flower.form: An open, slightly cupped flower sitting tight against the shoot
flower.centre: Twenty to thirty stamens with pink filaments and orange-red anthers around a single style, in a reddish cup
flower.behind: A reddish-brown cup with five small rounded sepals
flower.carried: Singly or in pairs on very short stalks, crowded along last year's bare shoots, well before the leaves
flower.season: March to early April, early enough to need frost cover

fruit: A drupe like a peach but with smooth, hairless, shiny skin: round, 5 to 7 cm, with a groove down one side. Pale yellow or greenish-white ground largely flushed crimson. A single deeply pitted stone. Sits almost stalkless against the shoot. Ripe August to September. Fruit set: small smooth green fruitlets tight against the shoot.
seedling: Not drawn: grown as grafted trees
winter: Bare fan or small tree: smooth reddish shoots with the buds in threes at many nodes, a fat round flower bud either side of a slim pointed leaf bud.

leaf: long narrow lance-shaped leaf with a long fine point
glossy, hairless, often folded and arching
bloom: pink-stalked stamens with orange-red anthers around a single style
flower stalkless against a bare shoot
young: a small open tree or wall fan
dormant: bare reddish shoots, a small open tree or wall fan
buds in threes at the nodes
flower: pink blossom crowded along bare shoots
no leaves yet, or only tiny ones
set: small smooth green fruitlets tight against the shoots
long narrow young leaves around them
crop: round smooth shiny fruit, red over yellow, no fuzz
fruit sitting close against the shoot

look_alikes: Peach is the same plant with downy fruit. Almond has paler blossom and a flat, dry, downy fruit. Apricot has broad round leaves and white or pale pink flowers. Ornamental cherries carry their flowers on long stalks in bunches.
